... SECOND INNINGS ...

The Sri Lankan bowlers struggled to contain the Bangladesh batters but showed resilience towards the end of Day 2. Asitha Fernando took 4 wickets while Tharindu Rathnayake and Milan Rathnayake each claimed 3 wickets. Prabath Jayasuriya remained wicketless. With the batting-friendly pitch likely to pose challenges for the Bangladesh bowlers as well, the contest remains wide open. As Sri Lanka embarks on their innings, the spotlight shifts to their ability to navigate the pitch and post a competitive total against Bangladesh's mammoth score. Stay tuned for the Sri Lankan innings in a short while...

Bangladesh end their innings at a mammoth 495 runs, building on the solid foundation laid by Najmul Hossain Shanto, Litton Das, and Mushfiqur Rahim. The pair of Mushfiqur and Shanto recorded a 247-run partnership on Day 1, helping Bangladesh recover from 45/3 to 292/3 at stumps. Resuming on Day 2, they continued their dominance, with Shanto falling just short of 150. Rahim scored 163 before being given out LBW, and Litton Das scored 90 before following suit. The rest of the batters couldn't do much but they will be on the happier side at the end of their innings.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin! The sun is out, and let's hope it stays this way. The umpires and the players make their way out in the middle. Hasan Mahmud and Nahid Rana will resume their innings. The tail will look to get to that 500 run mark! Asitha Fernando will start the proceedings with the ball. Let's play...

Russell Arnold is pitchside. He says that there are a few cracks in the middle and it can pose a problem for the Sri Lankan batters. He says that the seamers will get some assistance, and they will need to attack accordingly.

Mushfiqur Rahim is in for a chat. He says that the wicket was good to bat on and he had a chat with Najmul Hossain Shanto that they need to be positive and move on. He says that he needs to keep up with he fitness of the youngsters and he works on it. Ends by saying that the wicket is good and they need to bowl well.

With batting-friendly conditions here, it will be a fascinating battle between the bowlers and batters. And with rain forecasted, let's hope it stays away and we get to see some great cricket on Day 3! Stay tuned...

The spotlight will now shift to Sri Lanka's response, and they will look to bundle the visitors and challenge their mammoth total. Bangladesh's bowlers, after their innings, will look to build on their momentum and bowl Sri Lanka out cheaply, while the Lankans will aim to see off the new ball and build a solid foundation.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks! Day 3 promises to be thrilling as Bangladesh will look to push their score and get over 500 run mark. After a strong batting display, Bangladesh will be pleased with their score of 484/9 at stumps, with Najmul Hossain Shanto, Litton Das, and Mushfiqur Rahim setting the tone. The Rathnayake brothers, Milan and Tharindu, played a crucial role in Sri Lanka's evening session fightback, with Milan claiming 3 quick wickets towards the end.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

Make no mistake, 484 is still a formidable total, but Bangladesh will be slightly disappointed if they are bowled out without crossing the 500-run mark. Sri Lanka, meanwhile, will be keen to wrap up the final wicket quickly and shift focus to their batting response. It will be interesting to see how the pitch plays on Day 3, especially with more rain in the forecast. To make up for the lost time, play on Day 3 will begin 15 minutes earlier than usual at 4.15 am GMT. Until then, take care and goodbye!

Once play resumed, the hosts returned with renewed purpose and finally found the breakthroughs they had been searching for all day. The rain seemed to have injected some life into what had been a pretty docile surface until that point. It was Asitha Fernando who gave Sri Lanka the opening by trapping Mushfiqur in front, and soon after, Litton fell for 90. From there, Milan Rathnayake got in on the act, picking up three wickets. From a commanding position at 458 for 4, Bangladesh ended the day at 484 for 9, losing 5 wickets for just 26 runs.

We got just about an hour of play in the second session before rain intervened. In that brief passage, the two batters looked increasingly assured at the crease. Just before the rain arrived, Sri Lanka had a close LBW shout against Mushfiqur Rahim, but the on-field decision of not out was upheld on review, with the Ball Tracking showing umpire’s call. That encapsulated Sri Lanka’s frustrating, largely fruitless outing up to that point. However, fortunes shifted after the lengthy rain delay.

Earlier in the day, Bangladesh resumed on 292 with Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim at the crease. However, Shanto couldn’t survive the first hour. Mushfiqur then joined forces with Litton Das to pile on the runs, with Litton playing the more aggressive role. Sri Lanka had a couple of run-out opportunities during the stand, and to make matters worse, Pathum Nissanka dropped a catch when Das was on 14.

The light meter is out, and the players are walking off. While the umpires haven’t officially called it a day yet, it’s hard to see the light improving enough at this time of day for any further play. And it's official, it is STUMPS on Day 2. A much-improved session for Sri Lanka, and Dhananjaya de Silva will be pleased with how his side responded after a long grind. They picked up 5 wickets for just 61 runs in the 20.4 overs that were possible in the session.

Commentary.Commentary: And we're back underway after a lengthy rain interruption! The play can go up to 1 pm GMT if the weather and light allow. The umpires and the players make their way out in the middle. Litton Das and Mushfiqur Rahim will resume their innings. Milan Rathnayake will continue. Let's play...

UPDATE - 10.33 am GMT - We have a resumption time, folks! Play is set to resume at 10.45 am GMT. It will be interesting to see how Bangladesh go about the upcoming passage of play. Considering the amount of time lost today and rain in the forecast over the next three days, they might look to press on the accelerator.
UPDATE - 10.27 am GMT - The stumps have been erected and the umpires are out for an inspection. These are promising signs, and it should not be long before we get back underway. Stick around!

UPDATE - 10.15 am GMT - The ground staff are working tirelessly to get the ground ready for action, and we await further word on when play might resume. It is always a challenge to ensure the entire ground is covered properly, and once the rain stops, the key is to prevent the water collected on the covers from running onto the playing surface. Stay tuned for more news!

UPDATE - 9.49 am GMT - Good news! The rain has subsided and the ground staff have made their way out to the centre. The tyres placed on top of the covers to prevent them from being blown away are being removed first, after which the ground staff will begin clearing any water off the covers.
UPDATE - 9.42 am GMT - The last we heard from the ground was that the heavy rain had reduced to a persistent drizzle. Let’s hope it stops completely soon so we can get some play in the final session.
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

It is still raining and TEA has been taken on Day 2.  We only had an hour of play in the second session and whatever play we had, it belonged to Bangladesh. It had been a combination of pace from one end and spin from the other, but Sri Lanka struggled to create even a half chance in that hour after Lunch. The surface offered little to no assistance, and Litton Das and Mushfiqur Rahim found it all too easy to keep the scoreboard ticking. The radar indicates that the weather is clearing up, and hopefully we will get back on the park for the final session of the day.

Any football fans in the house? The English Premier League fixtures are out, and it starts on 15th August. Both Arsenal and Manchester United face daunting starts in their EPL season opener. Arsenal's schedule includes away games at Manchester United and Liverpool, plus home ties against Leeds, Nottingham Forest, and Manchester City. However, United's fixture list might be even more challenging, featuring top-four teams Arsenal, Manchester City, and Chelsea, along with away and home games against Fulham and Burnley, respectively.

UPDATE - 8.46 am GMT - It continues to rain in Galle, and to make matters worse, the intensity has picked up. We had hoped it would be a passing shower, but that does not seem to be the case. The wait for the weather to clear continues.

UPDATE - 8.12 am GMT - The ground staff are ready with the covers, and here they come. It’s just a light drizzle for now, but the clouds look grey and threatening. The atmosphere has certainly turned, and we might be in for a bit of a delay if this persists. The good thing is that in this part of the world, they cover the entire ground, so if the rain does ease up, the resumption should not take too long.

As the second session approaches, Sri Lanka will look to regroup and strategize to break the Bangladesh partnership. Can they engineer a crucial breakthrough and shift the momentum in their favor? With Rahim and Das looking solid at the crease, the Lankans will need to be sharp and innovative to make an impact. Stay tuned as we will be back in a short while post the Lunch break...

The Sri Lankan bowlers have struggled to make breakthroughs, despite enjoying some half-chances. The pacer Asitha Fernando got the only wicket of the Bangladesh skipper in this session. The spin duo of Tharindu Rathnayake and Prabath Jayasuriya have been working hard, but Bangladesh's batters have played disciplined cricket.

SESSION SUMMARY -  27 overs, 91 runs, and 1 wicket. Bangladesh continues to dominate this Test, building on the solid foundation laid on Day 1. The partnership between Mushfiqur Rahim and Najmul Hossain Shanto set the tone for a commanding performance on the first day. They continued well coming into Day 2, but Shanto fell just short of a 150. Rahim remains steadfast, now batting on 141, while Litton Das has joined forces with Rahim, currently standing at 43 and taking an aggressive approach. Bangladesh's current score stands at a mammoth 383/4.

Commentary.Commentary: The sun is shining in all its glory and we are all set to get going on Day 2. Dhananjaya de Silva and his men make their way out to the centre, followed by the two overnight batters of Bangladesh, Mushfiqur Rahim and Najmul Hossain Shanto. Asitha Fernando will open the attack for the hosts. Rahim to face. Two slips and a gully in place. Away we go!

PITCH REPORT - Farveez Maharoof is near the deck. Informs that there has been an average of 2.7 degrees of turn when the ball lands in line with the stumps, and 3.4 degrees when it lands outside the stump line. The spinners would be wise to focus on those areas, especially from one end where a rough patch has formed due to the bowlers’ footmarks, along with another area that’s starting to wear on a shorter length. Mentions that these are still good batting conditions, and if Bangladesh can get to somewhere around 450–500, they will be in a strong position.

Angelo Mathews is in for a chat. Mentions that his decision to retire was not sudden, but the result of several factors coming together. He says his recent performances were not up to expectations and he did not want to become a burden on the team. Mathews also points to the scheduling, explaining that playing just one Test and then stepping away would allow his replacement to immediately get game time rather than wait. He states that his only regret is not reaching the milestone of 10,000 Test runs, a target he believed he could achieve. Despite that, he shares that he has given everything he had to Sri Lankan cricket and walks away with immense pride. Shares that he is looking forward to making a strong case for himself for the 2026 T20 World Cup.

For Sri Lanka, it was a tough day in the field, though not entirely unexpected given how the early days here generally favour batters. Once the ball softened, they found it hard to maintain pressure. In fact, just 2 maiden overs across 64 overs of spin paint a clear picture of their struggles to build sustained pressure. The second new ball is only 10 overs old, so there should still be some assistance for the bowlers if they hit the right areas. Can Sri Lanka make early inroads this morning and turn things around? Stick around, as the first ball on Day 2 is not far away.

Bangladesh won the toss but made a shaky start, slipping to 45/3. However, Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim came together to steady the innings and repair the early damage. The pair stitched an unbeaten 247-run stand, with both batters notching up centuries in batting-friendly conditions. Their partnership has set up the visitors nicely, especially considering the history of this venue where batting last is often a daunting task. They will now look to build further and post a massive first innings total.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the first Test between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh in Galle. It was a day of dominance for the visitors on Day 1, as they controlled proceedings for the better part of the day. We were treated to uninterrupted action on the opening day, and the weather looks good for more of the same today.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Bangladesh, of course, will be the dominant side heading into the sheds, as not only have they got a good amount of runs on the first day, but also they do have enough wickets in hand to stretch the score further, with two proper batters to follow next. But one thing is for certain, once this pitch starts to bite, it will be a landmine for the batters and to have big runs on the board in the first innings, will always benefit the batting side. However, we have time and again seen Bangladesh slipping off collapses, and come Day 2, they will aim to prevent that this time around. For Sri Lanka, it is all about picking quick wickets the next day, coming with a fresh energy and intensity, to avoid Bangladesh run away with a huge score. The first ball on Day 2 will be bowled at 4.30 am GMT, on Wednesday, 18th June. But our build up will begin well in advance. Till then, take care, cheers!

This partnership was a very crucial one, not only from Bangladesh’s point of view, as they were in early trouble, losing three wickets on just 45, but in context of form of Shanto and Rahim as well. The two weren’t in the best of nick coming into this series, but their unbeaten 247-run stand has helped their confidence big time. Particularly Rahim, who was coming off a very lean patch since quite a few innings, and the one who loves to play against Sri Lanka, and has scored the most runs than any opposition, with a healthy average. He scored his fourth century against Sri Lanka, while Najmul Hossain Shanto, the skipper, too made his presence effective with a remarkable century of his own.

It looked like Sri Lanka was more on the defensive in the third session, trying to bowl as many dots to stem the run flow, as the two batters milked ones and twos with absolute ease. The pitch had no demons on it, and the ball came really well onto the bat, to which Shanto and Rahim made hay with the sunshine and just didn’t look uncomfortable for one bit. On such a pitch that is so docile, the Lankan bowlers lacked a bit in variation, which made them a bit too predictable as well.

As it has been the trend at Galle, you see a lot of spin throughout the day, as pacers come for a short burst here and there. The same happened today as well as out of 90 overs, 64 overs were bowled by the spinners. But they too, failed to make any impact and even the ‘Galle’dozer, Prabath Jayasuriya, was dealt with ease, and Tharindu Rathnayake, though picked up two wickets, went for runs as the batters just didn’t allow him to settle with his lines and lengths. The two batters were very effective with their slog sweeps and paddles and anything loose offered was put away as well.

Barring the first hour in the first session, where the ball did the talking with some lateral movement and a bit of turn, it has been a barren period for the bowlers as they have toiled hard throughout the day in desperate need of wickets, but have got zero assistance from the surface. It has appeared to be a haven for the batters and the two experienced campaigners in Mushfiqur Rahim and Najmul Hossain Shanto looked completely untroubled through and through, bailing Bangladesh out of a precarious 45/3.

A job very well done by Bangladesh with the bat, and the day belongs well and truly to the visitors as they have gone unbeaten for two straight sessions, without losing a single wicket. Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the third and final session of the day. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the centre. Tharindu Rathnayake will get us underway with the ball. Mushfiqur Rahim to face. Let's play...

The pair looked largely untroubled, and apart from a half-chance when Rahim was on 25, they batted with complete assurance. To be fair, the odd ball has turned, but otherwise, the pitch has been flat, and with the ball getting softer, it has become a real grind for the bowlers. Bangladesh have suffered collapses in the recent past, and Sri Lanka will believe that if they can break this stand early after Tea, they might just be able to spark another. Do join us back at 9.30 am GMT for the start of the third session.

Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim picked up right where they left off before the Lunch break. They used their feet and the crease expertly, ensuring they didn’t get bogged down and kept the scoreboard ticking with ones and twos. At the same time, they were quick to put away anything loose. Tharindu Rathnayake, in particular, was not allowed to settle, and even Prabath Jayasuriya struggled to find any rhythm or build pressure by consistently targeting one batter.

92 runs in 30 overs without losing a wicket - A dominant session for Bangladesh, just what the doctor ordered after being 45/3 in the morning session. It was a session of real toil for Sri Lanka. Despite the heavy use of spin in the session, the spinners managed just one maiden between them, highlighting how well Bangladesh batted and how tough it’s been for the hosts to apply any sustained pressure.
Too slow, and on the leg stump line. Mushfiqur Rahim flicks this easily to deep mid-wicket for a single. And that will be TEA ON DAY 1!

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. Bangladesh has made a brilliant comeback after being reduced to 45/3 in the first session. Under extremely good conditions to bat on, both Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim have looked solid and fluent, forming a crucial partnership, with both in touching distance to get their fifties. It’s been a mix of pace and spin from Sri Lanka, but so far, it hasn’t produced success. Also, there haven’t been many maiden overs, only four to be exact in 43 overs, and all by pacers, which proves that the two batters have been busy and haven’t gone into a shell. The session so far has gone Bangladesh’s way and Sri Lanka needs to break this stand as quickly as possible to get some momentum back. Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the post-Lunch session. It was quite sunny out there in the opening session, but the overhead conditions have gotten a bit cloudy now, with the sun peeking out of the clouds. There's rain in the forecast, but we hope it stays away. Nothing threatening at all as of now as the sky looks blue with scattered clouds from one end. Out come Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim to resume their batting. Tharindu Rathnayake (10-0-52-2) to begin with the ball. Here we go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

Two seasoned campaigners now occupy the crease, and for Mushfiqur Rahim, this could be a defining moment. The veteran batter, who’s endured a lean spell over his last 13 innings, averaging under 20, has a golden chance to rediscover his touch and guide Bangladesh out of troubled waters. He has looked good so far and has got a decent start as well, and will look to convert it into an inning of substance for his side. The skipper too, will aim to bat long as with a long tail to follow, this Shanto-Rahim stand will be very crucial for the tourists. The second session is often the best window to bat on, especially under sunny skies. But if Sri Lanka strike early after the break, the pressure on the tourists will escalate quickly. The post-Lunch session will begin at 7.10 am GMT. Stay tuned.

To be very fair, the pitch didn’t show any kind of demons on it and was a pretty good one to bat on, with proper sunny conditions, but it was the execution of the Sri Lankan bowlers that brought them success early. Prabath Jayasuriya, whose record in Galle is more than stellar, constantly bowled on tight lines. But the experienced pair of Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim formed a responsible partnership to see through the session as batting got a bit easier.

Shadman Islam and Mominul Haque showed good discipline with the bat, digging in to stitch together a steadying stand. With only two pacers at their disposal, Sri Lanka were quick to turn to spin. Prabath Jayasuriya almost immediately challenged the batters with spin, while Tharindu Rathnayake, on debut, looked very composed and precise with the ball, eventually taking two quick wickets, which pegged Bangladesh on the back foot early doors.

It was an intriguing first session where, despite the batting-friendly nature of the surface, the ball managed to stay just ahead. True to the pre-match chatter, there was plenty on offer for the quicks, and Sri Lanka’s pace duo of Milan Rathnayake and Asitha Fernando were right on the money. Fernando struck early with disciplined lines and lengths, aided by some movement off the seam and the breeze that tested the batters' resilience.

SESSION SUMMARY - 28 overs, 90 runs, 3 wickets - Hmm... Almost a balanced opening session of this opening Test, or rather, shall we say, the Angelo Mathews Test! But, with three wickets falling, it slightly gives an edge to Sri Lanka. The first half of the session saw the ball dominating the bat, but as the session progressed, batting looked comparatively easier. A good over rate by the home side with the ball. And as they say, when in Sri Lanka, you will be treated with a lot of spin, which is proven right. Only 9 overs of pace bowled with 19 overs bowled by spinners so far on Day 1.

Commentary.Commentary: The sun is out and we are all set to get going. Angelo Mathews is given a guard of honour by his teammates. They are followed by the two openers of Bangladesh, Shadman Islam and Anamul Haque. Asitha Fernando will open the attack for the hosts. Shadman to face. Two slips and a gully in place. Here we go!

We are moments away from the first ball, but before that, it is time for the national anthems. Dhananjaya de Silva and Najmul Hossain Shanto lead their respective sides out. It will be the national anthem of Bangladesh first, followed by that of Sri Lanka.

PITCH REPORT - Farveez Maharoof is pitchside. He begins by pointing out that the sun has been playing a bit of hide and seek and also highlights that there was a bit of rain around as well in the morning. Observes that it is very hard underneath with barely any grass covering on it. Mentions that spinners will come into play in the second or the third day and also feels that the batters will enjoy playing their strokes on this surface. Reckons that there won’t be much turn on the first day and it will belong to the batters.

Time for a felicitation ceremony for Angelo Mathews. His family members are beside him as he is presented with a memento by the Sri Lankan cricket board. Mathews walks up for a quick chat. He begins by saying that he can’t believe the amount of love that he is getting. Thanks the Almighty, and also appreciates his family members and friends for supporting him in his journey through thick and thin. Mentions that he is extremely proud of this journey and feels special to have played over 100 Tests for Sri Lanka. Adds that playing for the country was his dream and he is glad that it came true. Ends by saying that he is happy to be a part of the journey that Sri Lankan cricket has had over the last decade.
Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Shadman Islam, Anamul Haque, Mominul Haque, Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Mushfiqur Rahim, Litton Das (WK), Jaker Ali, Taijul Islam, Hasan Mahmud, Nahid Rana, Nayeem Hasan.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Lahiru Udara (On debut), Dinesh Chandimal, Angelo Mathews, Kamindu Mendis, Dhananjaya de Silva (C), Kusal Mendis (WK), Milan Rathnayake, Tharindu Rathnayake (On debut), Prabath Jayasuriya, Asitha Fernando.

The skipper of Sri Lanka, Dhananjaya de Silva, says he also would have batted first, pointing to the recent trend at Galle where teams prefer to bat first. Mentions that the surface looks different and feels that it will favour the batters more. States that Angelo Mathews has been one of the greatest players Sri Lanka has ever produced.

The captain of Bangladesh, Najmul Hossain Shanto, says that the wicket looks very dry and he believes that batting first is an ideal choice. Reckons that the spinners will get good assistance in the fourth innings and a chance to pick up all the wickets. Highlights that they have good memories from the last Test against Zimbabwe, but also adds that this is a new game with new conditions. Stresses about playing good cricket. Informs that they are going with seven batters, two spinners and two pacers.
TOSS - Bangladesh have won the toss and they will BAT first.

Bangladesh, who finished one spot below Sri Lanka in the last cycle, had moments to savour. A historic 2-0 series win in Pakistan and a drawn series in the West Indies were standout achievements. While the ODI captaincy has shifted to Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Najmul Hossain Shanto continues to lead the Test side. However, Mehidy’s availability for the opener is in doubt due to illness. It would be a blow for the tourists if he misses out, particularly with the surface expected to aid spinners. That said, there is rain forecast for all five days of the Test, which could bring the pacers into play. Let's hope that the rain stays away. Toss and team news coming up shortly...

For Sri Lanka, the previous WTC cycle was a tale of missed chances. Three wins from their final four Tests would have secured a spot in the final, but they lost all four. Now, with Dimuth Karunaratne retired and this being Angelo Mathews’ final Test, a new era is about to begin. Captain Dhananjaya de Silva and his men will be keen to give Mathews a fitting farewell. And when you talk about Galle, Prabath Jayasuriya is a name that instantly comes up. The left-arm spinner has been lethal here, with 80 wickets in 19 innings and 9 of his 11 five-wicket hauls coming at this venue.

Waking up today brought that familiar feeling, like the first day of a new school year or a new job. The dust has barely settled on South Africa's drought-breaking World Test Championship final win over Australia, and already we are set for the beginning of a new WTC cycle. Two Asian rivals, whose battles have grown more intense in recent years, especially in white ball cricket, now turn their attention to the red ball game. They meet in a two-match Test series to launch the 2025-27 WTC cycle. On that note, hello and welcome to the first Test between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh at the picturesque Galle International Stadium.
